subtype: Approach: reporting to the school lost and found [Action]
passage: I'm Rehana, and Bhupen sits behind me in class. Yesterday it got cold and he came without his sweater. At the break he went to the office, where the peon keeps a big box of lost things. Bhupen described it: grey, with a stripe on the sleeve. "And my name is inside the collar." The peon looked through the box and found it. The peon checked the name against the one Bhupen said. Then the peon handed it over. I could not tell what Bhupen felt, but he put it on and buttoned it up straight away.

qa.q: What did Bhupen tell the peon about his sweater?
qa.a: He said it was grey, with a stripe on the sleeve and his name inside the collar.

qa.q: What might Bhupen have been feeling as he put the sweater on and buttoned it up?
qa.a: He was probably relieved and glad to be warm again. Rehana can only guess, because Bhupen said little.

qa.q: What could Bhupen do so his sweater does not go missing again, and why?
qa.a: He could hang it on the same hook each day. The name in the collar already helps, but a fixed hook means he can find it faster.

qa.q: How does the peon see Bhupen's request?
qa.a: The peon has a clear description and a name to check, so it is easy to find the right sweater and hand it back without a mix-up.

grounding: A boy who loses his sweater goes to the office lost and found, describes it and the name inside, and the peon returns it.

subtype: Approach: reporting to the school lost and found [Action]
passage:
Monday. Kunal came home shivering. His grey sweater was gone, left somewhere after the sports period. "The new one?" his big sister Irawati asked, and he nodded, miserable.
Tuesday. At recess Kunal went to the office. "I lost a sweater. Grey, one blue stripe, and KUNAL M. written inside the collar." Ramesh bhaiya, the peon, dug through the lost property box. "Not yet. Come back."
Thursday. Ramesh bhaiya found Kunal in the corridor, holding up a grey sweater. "Blue stripe. KUNAL M." Kunal pulled it on right there.

qa.q: What was written inside the sweater's collar?
What was Kunal feeling on Monday?
qa.a: He came home shivering and nodded miserably, so he felt upset and worried about losing the new sweater.

qa.q: What made Kunal's report work, and what else could he try?
qa.a: Describing the colour, stripe and name helped the peon recognise it; he could also ask the sports teacher, since it went missing after the sports period.

qa.q: How might Ramesh bhaiya see Kunal's description?
qa.a: With a clear colour, stripe and name, Ramesh bhaiya could match the sweater easily and bring it straight to Kunal.

grounding: Shows a boy reporting a lost sweater at the office lost and found, describing it and the name inside, and the peon returning it.

subtype: Approach: reporting to the school lost and found [Action]
passage: Gurpreet, you ask why I stitch your name into every jersey? Listen to your Dadaji Jeevan. When I was ten, in Amritsar, I lost the maroon sweater my mother had knitted all winter. I was afraid to tell her. A classmate said, 'Go to the office, there's a box.' So I went, knees shaking, and told the clerk: maroon, cable pattern, and my name, J-E-E-V-A-N, stitched in white thread inside the neck. The peon, old Harnam, lifted out a heap of caps and mufflers, then held up my sweater. 'This one has a name. Easy,' he said. I ran home wearing it.

qa.q: What did the lost sweater look like?
qa.a: It was maroon, with a cable pattern and the name stitched in white thread inside the neck.

qa.q: Why were young Jeevan's knees shaking at the office?
qa.a: He was afraid, both of losing the sweater his mother had knitted all winter and of having to tell her.

qa.q: Which choice in the story helped most, and why?
qa.a: Going to the office and describing the sweater and the stitched name, because it let the peon pick it out of a heap straight away.

qa.q: How did Harnam see the sweater with the name?
qa.a: For Harnam a name made the job simple; he said 'This one has a name. Easy' and handed it back.

grounding: Illustrates a boy going to the school office's lost and found, describing his sweater and the name inside, and the peon returning it.
